channel.title: The Spanish Chapter: Resetting Everything, Once Again | The Kalen Michael Experiment
channel.description: Packing up, unpacking a new life, and learning how to navigate the vibrant streets, language, and culture of Spain's capital after a total reset.

item.title: Be Grateful for the Challenges
item.content:encoded: I have had a very interesting last 3 months. It has become clear that I have not been making the best decisions in my life and I am now left dealing with the repercussions of these choices. My biggest challenge of late has been trying to get myself balanced. I regularly find myself challenged and the thought crosses my mind to give up and to move towards the victim mentality. It was a little bit of a coping mechanism in the past and the challenge is now to break the habit. I am pushing myself to be grateful for the things that I do have, as well as reminding myself that even without anything just being alive is a blessing. Life comes with many experiences, some good, some bad, but none of which you could experience if you were not alive. I have plans for the future, I have some ideas and I am taking steps to reach them. The path is not clear as of yet, but I am working on it everyday and trying to ensure that my decisions are leading me where I intend to go. I remember thinking in a past moment that it would be interesting to see where life will be taking me. I find myself thinking the same again, as though I have finally awoken from a long nap and I am now ready to take action. One thing I have noticed is that the hard times in my life tend to attract me towards comfort. The more stress I am experiencing the more I want to indulge in things that I normally would believe to not be great for me. It is a fine line that we walk in this life, and it seems that at any moment we could vere off into another direction. For this reason I remain diligent and hopeful of the future.

item.title: I Have a Life
item.content:encoded: It’s a strange thing looking back at days past. I’ve been going through my old photos clearing up the ones that mean nothing in an attempt to create an album that I will actually use. Some memories are good and make me happy, but others bring sadness. People I have lost, people who are still alive but we no longer speak. Some of them we just lost contact because of time, others hearts I broke, or perhaps my drunken behaviour forced them to leave. I know that I can never go back, that changing the past is not possible and the only step forward is to learn from it. The sadness and pain of longing makes me crave a cigarette, or some beer. Anything to take away the feeling that hits me at this moment. How I would love to share my love with those that used to exist in my life in days past. I hope that one day we meet again, in a new world with forgiveness in our hearts ready to start a new. I miss you all.

item.title: Sunrise/Sunset
item.content:encoded:
It’s a funny thing life. The consistency of the battle that is. It seems that no matter what I do to get myself back up, I eventually find myself down again. Down and questioning but what is the point. But are we asking ourselves the right questions?

Is there truly a point to life. Inevitably we are all going to leave this plane of existence, one way or another depending on your beliefs. Nothing we collect in this life will come with us, perhaps not even our memories and experiences. Its as if our entire existence will be wiped clean on our deathbeds, or at the very least once the last person on earth remembers our name.

If we cannot control this common fact, what can we control? Perhaps only the years in between. The dash on your gravestone. Surely we have control over this. However, many of us find ourselves continuing to live an existence that does not fulfill us. Doing things purely to help the clock tick, living as if we will live forever.

What would over lives mean if we seized every opportunity, lived every moment, smiled at every stranger. What unbelievable tap would we open, what abundance would come pouring into our lives.

For just 1 week witness the sunrise and the sunset everyday and see how it changes you!

item.title: Commiting to the Grind
item.content:encoded: I have been slowly finding my way again. Step by step, brick by brick, moving forward, building myself up. It is hard to explain how good it feels to be on the right track, one thousand times or more better than over indulging as I did before. It’s more difficult that’s for sure. I find myself reading labels again and with less choices in my purchases since changing to eating plant based. Waking up at 6am can be tough but not nearly as tough as going to bed at 22:00. Step by step, brick by brick. I am growing and proud to be improving. I will grind until the day I die, I will be the best version of me possible.

item.title: Relationship Patterns
item.content:encoded:
Here I am, coming out of my second relationship in 8 months. I jumped straight from one into another and followed the same patterns. It’s clear to me that I need to do some serious work on myself before I undertake another one. I did some research and I am showing signs of emotional immaturity. So here it goes. Here are the things you should watch out for next time you enter a relationship.

  1. Don’t fall to early, give the relationship time to grow. Chances are if you fall to early it’s not real attraction but the fulfillment of some unfulfilled need.
  2. Don’t break up too soon. Relationships are hard work. If you want to break up every time things get hard, then your not ready to be in one.
  3. Don’t be needy. A healthy person realises that everyone needs their space. Make sure not to demand too much time. Be available not demanding.
  4. Make arguments productive. If an argument is not going to be productive there is really no need to have it, and if you have many unproductive arguments it might be time to look inward. It takes two to argue.

So today I am starting fresh. The rebirth of Kalen Michael. It’s difficult for me to look back at the last year and how far I fell from my ideal self. At the time it seemed like I would never fall this low again. Yet here I am, making the same mistakes, living the same poor lifestyle choices. It’s ironic. But today it changes. Today I am starting fresh, the new me will become what the old me once was, only better. I woke up at 6am and went for a run, then I had a meditation session. At 9am I will head out to meet Alan, my business partner, so we can make some sales. Today I get back on track, I am going to forget about women for awhile until I am strong enough to be who I need to be.

item.title: Like a Moth to the Flame
item.content:encoded:
Recently I have fallen short of my goals. My to do lists vanished for about a month and I found myself doing much less than normal. My exercise routine dropped to once per week, yoga became erratic, and I haven’t read much in the last month. Depression was closely shadowing me, and whether the lack of goalkeeping was causing the depression or the depression was causing the lack of goalkeeping, I found myself achieving less than expected. My diet suffered too as meals became less regular and I ate out more often.

I spent the last 3 days in bed recovering from a cold which gave me time to think and internalise something. This has given me the courage to begin building myself back up to where I was two months ago. This entry is to serve as a reminder that sometimes we fall down, but we can always get back up again!

item.title: I Find my Passion
item.content:encoded:
Recently I have felt uneasy about the goals I set myself some months ago. I decided that it was time to consolidate the goals I have set into my life long purpose. It is possible this will change over the coming months, years, or decades. Yet with this new purpose I feel at ease.

“I want for nothing. Everything I need and want is made available for me at the right moment. In every situation, I offer the best of myself. I give my best of me to everyone I meet. Guided by meditation and self-discovery I give through my heart, my soul and my passion. Everyday and in everyway, I work towards my goals. I never give up. I connect people. I help them to express their inner identities by shining a light on the goodness. I remind people of their inner beauty and of their potential, in the process, I discovered my own. I train the Mind and the Body. Mind is improved through meditation, reading, affirmations and correct mindset. Body is improved through healthy vegan nutrition, calisthenics and yoga. Body and Mind are jointly trained with cold showers, minimalism, and no fap. I live a life of love and compassion. I am love. And so it is!”

item.title: My World Gets Darker
item.content:encoded:
Momentum has slowed down and what was easy is beginning to seem a little more difficult. My iron will power has begun to chip and it shows signs of being hollow. I question myself what could be bringing this about. I sleep more, much more. Unaware whether I am tired or whether I am escaping a short rest turns into a several hour sleep. I remind myself of the cycle of my life.

Could it be my diet that is causing these changes as it has definitely begun to falter. Perhaps it is the mental changes as my brain begins to consolidate the ideas of religion into my ones agnostic paradigms. I try not to cling and remind myself that this too will pass.

item.title: Spiritual Path
item.content:encoded:
I find myself in an interesting position. It has been many years since I have considered devotion to a God. I have been agnostic and even vengeful to the idea of a God. My mind is tangled with confusion as it attempts to understand what it happening. My quest for worldly fulfillment has brought me full course back to spirituality. I find many ideas easy to accept as my Self-Development journey express many of the same concepts. Could it be that spirituality is the glue that holds it all together?

I do not feel this to be a passing fad. It is becoming clear that I am being called to religion, to spirituality, to God. With each passing moment I can feel the pull becoming stronger along with my desire to dedicate myself to a life of study and meditation. My struggle is in connecting my worldly ambitions with those of the divine.

It will be interesting to watch as this path unfolds, the discovery is thrilling. Who will I be at the next intersection of my life? The question both excites and scares me. This is a profound change in my beliefs and attitudes. This will surely redirect the course of my life. I find myself praying to the Divine Mother for guidance, an act I would not have even entertained in the not so distant past. “Free me from the illusion of this life, do with me as you will.”

item.title: Strange Occurences
item.content:encoded:
I find myself in an interesting place at the moment. With my recent efforts towards self-improvement and realisation I had begun to neglect my meditation. Seeking to replace it with the time spent in Yoga and Pranayama. I completed my first round of chosen guide books which I had categorised as follows: The 4 hour workweek by Tim Ferris - Freedom Think and Grow Rich by Napoleon Hill - Wealth How to Win Friends and Influence People by Dale Carnegie - Relationships Psycho-Cybernetics by Max Maxwell - Mindset At the time of completion I did not think much of this and decided to read an unrelated book before starting my second round. While eating lunch, I was waiting for a YouTube video to load and an advert appeared that introduced me to Autobiography of a Yogi by Yogananda. The advert had such an effect on me that I began to investigate more about the book. On discovering that many prominent people had read this book, some many times, I decided to consider buying it. Find the book for £1.50 I promptly purchased it.

I have been deeply drawn to the book and reading it has been very easy even passing around two hours the second day of reading. Strangely I began to feel that this book should be added to my reading round as the Spiritual book. I imagined that it was the glue that held the others together. Interestingly there are many ideas that are shared with the other books of my reading round.

When the Vedic was mentioned I recalled my earlier friend explaining his vedic astrology to me. At the time I didn’t listen much as I found astrology to be a topic not worth my time. This book sparked my interest and I decided to get my chart done. After reading my chart I felt devoid of energy and took a long nap. When I eventually woke up I was urged to continue reading the book which began promptly by explaining astrology and our ability to change what was written.

I am unsure what road I am being taken down but I believe myself to be in the right place.

item.title: When Easy Becomes Hard
item.content:encoded:
I’m approaching two months in Madrid. It’s been an interesting experience and I have come much further than I thought I would. I remember sitting in Turks and Caicos thinking I would never make it here in Spain. Focusing on all the potential things that would go wrong.

What’s strange is that my attitude has now shifted and now I find myself without any desire to return. I look back on my time in the Caribbean with an overall distaste. Despite all the beauty, it offered and the rescue from loneliness I was becoming someone other than me.

It took the spontaneous commitment to leave to turn that around. I felt myself returning almost as soon as I landed in Madrid airport. My first few weeks were spent very much idly hoping for the best. I took some action towards finding work and maintaining my mood. Yet mostly I just socialised and experienced my time in Spain.

Slowly the momentum built up and I found myself exercising daily and focusing more on my goals. After finding work and a room to rent the stability ensured I could focus more on self-improvement. I committed myself to read, practice yoga and meditate. These three activities became part of my morning routine and I did them as soon as I woke up every day. It was easy. Along with these I continued to exercise daily and only seemed to slack off on the occasional leg day. Leg workouts do not really excite me much, it is the exercises themselves that do not offer much in the way of excitement.

Over time the new and exciting exercises became normal and habit’s formed. Unfortunately with this came complacency. It became easier to take days off. This was the usual occurrence in my life. I would push myself hard for a period of time only to slowly revert to how things were before.

Not this time. This time I accept the challenge. Is it harder to continue?! At the moment, yes, I find it more difficult to stick to my goals. Yet that will not prevent me from giving it all I have. I will continue to push forward with the challenges I have set for myself.

I wanted to record this event as this is the exact moment in time I would normally give up. I would feel that I deserve a break and that break would become permanent. I have done this countless times in my life and I refuse to continue repeating the same life over and over again.

Today I declare that easy has become hard, and that hard will not break me. I will keep pushing on. I will keep working hard. I will succeed in my endeavours for I am the protagonist of my story. I create the life I want.

Often when we find something becoming difficult it is because we have forgotten to break down the task into smaller segments. Chunking is the way forward. It only takes one step to start a journey and another one step continues the very same.

I will conquer this challenge. Whether it takes me a day or a lifetime!

item.title: Money is Tight: Stretching whats left to Buy Time
item.description: I'm established but not yet stable, its going to take a little more work to make this sustainable.
item.content:encoded:
Spanish music plays silently in the background as I gaze out of the third floor window. Desert plants decorate the window sill and bring a sense of comfort. The room is painted in an Autumn style. Almost ironic as I look out into Summer.

Time is Flying By

In a few days I will have been in this bustling city for three weeks. The first week felt like it took a month to pass yet the following two passed as quickly as a meteor in the night sky. The rich culture and foreign language captivated the senses.

It was easy to be at peace in this moment, I had come far since arriving in Spain. With a backpack, €600, and a credit card already €800 in debt I started my adventure. I always knew that I was spending more than I had. Throughout my life I have not allowed myself to get into debt with financial institutions, opting rather to pay off any borrowed money before the interest set in. Yet I had been practicing daily to let go of these thoughts. To remain at peace despite my worries.

This time around it was not a luxury I could afford. I needed the cash to secure a rented room. And I would need to keep using the credit card until such time as my incomings surpassed my outgoings.

The Over Spender

I suppose I could have been more careful to start. Perhaps I ate out more often than I needed to. It was my first hostel accommodation that made budgeting difficult. The hostel was clean, safe, and warm. It offered most of what I needed. In fact it was this hostel that helped me to secure my first job, taking travelers out to eat Tapas. A traditional Spanish snack that is usually served alongside alcohol. The challenge at the time was the missing kitchen. Without a kitchen most of my meals were from restaurants. The vibrant vegan community in Madrid meant that I was not short of options. Having spent 3 months on a small island with little change, the diversity had my mouth watering.

When I eventually moved myself into a cheaper hostel and one that included a kitchen. I found that I could spend €4 for 5 days. This made a huge impact on my budgeting. I always remind myself not to look back, yet it’s hard not to see the savings I could have made from moving here first. Everything happens for a reason.

The difficulty of hostel life is that you find yourself never alone. 24 hours 7 days a week you have people around you. Your isolation mostly includes time in the bathroom. Even then there is always noise reminding you that you are not alone. The smells make sleeping interesting and there is always someone coming or going. Your sleep is never solid and you end up waking up several times throughout the night, every night.

Yet despite these challenges, it is humbling to have little more than a rented bed and a locker. Part unpacking and packing everyday. The truth of it is that in comparison to my 3 months cycling Western Europe this was luxury. Even the cold shower was better than no shower at all. I often find myself amazed at how little we really need. Once we lay down roots we begin to accumulate so many things and we truly believe we need them all. When you wake up with nothing more than what you can carry you feel truly free and you begin to question the origin of your thoughts before.

After three weeks I find myself here, finally alone. I managed to secure a rented room and with my part time work I am only making a loss of €65 per week.

I never really find myself feeling at home. At least in the traditional sense of settling down. I have however always loved Spain and the opportunity to pass some time here truly excites me.

The song on the radio changes and I’m back here in the present. One deep breathe follows the next. Happiness is truly a choice.

item.title: Settling In: The Beginnings of a New Life Start to Emerge
item.description: Life is getting established and its starting to feel a little more like a home.
item.content:encoded:
Waking up to chirping birds has become a regular occurrence. Occasionally the clashing of a glass in the distance meets the strum of a Spanish guitar, signaling the start of the day. It is always hot and for that my window remains open. I’m reminded that this is Spain.

I’m filled with a sense of pride when I think back on the few weeks I’ve been here.

Speaking in Foreign Tongues

Despite having traveled and even relocated many times, this is the first time I’ve attempted to settle somewhere where I cannot rely on my English. The 5 months I spent traveling through Spain in 2012 give me an obvious advantage. Even though my grammar needs some serious work, I am able to communicate. Sometimes I forget I’m not speaking my mother tongue.

Its a Trendy City

I find Madrid to be a fascinating city and I am particularly enamored with Retiro park. Drawn there on a daily basis to join in the athletic displays on the local calisthenic bars. Between sets, I find it exhilarating to watch the locals skateboard, roller-blade and even cycle backwards around the fountain in front of me.

The years I spent in London conditioned me to have a certain opinion of cities, an opinion which is quickly being shattered by the Spanish capital. Rather than the cosmopolitan display of suits and high fashion I find this city filled with trendy youth covered in tattoos and sporting interesting and unusual hairstyles. Perhaps I fit in here, walking around, Spotify blasting away on my headphones, it does feel like home.

Interesting Characters

In the weeks leading up to today, I managed to secure work, a place to live and navigate the confusing Spanish bureaucracy to obtain temporary legal status. I have been blessed to meet many amazing people. While many often move on to Barcelona, San Sebastián or even back towards their homes, I am truly grateful to have shared in their lives for just a moment.

Rohan, the friendly Indian who welcomed me on my first day in Madrid, embarked on his journey to share with his mother that he had been living a double life and was in-fact gay. He confided in me the irrational fear that arises from living in a country that does not allow people to be themselves. When he messaged me to say he was leaving Spain and his mother took the news well, I felt my heart skip a beat. For that short moment, I could share in his happiness. He could now be himself, if nowhere else at least at home.

Izabela, emancipated herself at 16, not because of family problems but because she craved independence and that paired with her intelligence enabled her to start university at that young age. Despite being only 21 as she sits across the table from me, I sense an old soul. With wisdom and compassion, she quotes many masters and shares her experiences traveling the world. She provides me with faith, faith that humanity can do better, that we can be better.

These are only two of the awe-inspiring characters I have met. Each unique individual inspiring me in some small way to be grateful for what I have, to fight for what I want and to never give up.

Feeling Thankful

This beautiful city, these wonderful people, they give me pride in my existence and I remain humble in this honour. How I wish I could share the blessings of this life with everyone I hold dear.

For now, know that I hold you all in my heart with me.

item.title: Leaving Home: Starting Over for the Third Time
item.description: Navigating the emotional turbulence of leaving home and stepping back into the unknown.
item.content:encoded:
Except for the two airport personnel, security was empty. Not something I usually experienced on international flights. After the usual undress and pat down I found myself in the departure terminal. Smaller than usual it was just what you would expect from such a small island.

This was it I was one step closer to leaving the place I called home for the last 3 months. It was a short time but it was with my dad and that made it home.

The Waiting Game

I identified the gate and put on some music. The intention was to drown out the thinking that inevitably occurs when you leave loved ones behind. But even distractions can only hold you for so long. The flight was delayed for unknown reasons and I eventually grew tired of the pacing and head bobbing. I retired to a chair. We finally began the boarding process and I found the music no longer offered me solace.

As the longing and reminiscing began it occurred to me that I had not yet left the island. Sitting in the plane I could see the small hills and fences that separated those leaving from those staying. Only a mere 10 minutes drive away was everything I now missed.

Take off took us over the roads I had been driving on and then over the areas I had worked and played. I held back the tears by reminding myself to look forward and not back. I could not undo the past but if the absence of this place, of these people, became unbearable I could always return.

Reflecting on Paradise

This island, this beautiful blue sea. I have been blessed to spend so much time in such an awe inspiring place. Surely I would find myself here again. As the memories flooded my mind I found myself battling the fear of the unknown, and perhaps the fear of missing out.

This was it, this was life. I’m sure one day I would look back at this very moment and find it to be an interesting story. Maybe it would teach me some life changing lessons or maybe I would just laugh at my naivety. For surely this was just a temporary trip away, like leaving home to buy bread only to return with more than you had when you left.

Growth and Characters

My time on paradise had taught me much. My flaws that had been pointed out and carved into my mind were now paths towards improvement. Unbelievable characters had introduced themselves. At times I felt like I was living in a ‘novella’. A short story about the island life and how you can choose to turn any situation into a blessing or a nightmare.

If grateful was a strong enough word I would use it. Yet it is found lacking in my appreciation for what has come my way in the recent months. And I only hope that I was worthy to receive such blessings.

Looking Forward

So out into the world I fly, crossing oceans, changing time zones and experiencing new cultures. In my heart, believing that once again those wonderful characters will make an appearance. And hopefully when they do, I will be able to give them back what they have given me, and then some.
